VERDICT: FINDINGS
GOAL: CANNOT TELL — the PROOF asks for the verdict line of "scripts/run-all-gates.sh --full", the summary lines of selftest.sh and init-test.sh, and a clean leak grep; none of those outputs is in the material, and F1 below is a way for kit-specific content to reach every adopting project.
F1 [P2] [important] harness.conf:29 (with scripts/init.sh:56, scripts/check-the-work.sh:849) — the kit points its own agent logs at the TEMPLATE folder that init copies verbatim into every new project. So the kit's own review, criterion and run rows ship into each adopter's docs/agents/*.jsonl, and so does its run history (kit file names, findings, model names). The adopter's proof audit then counts correction rows that are not its own — evidence: harness.conf sets HARNESS_AGENT_DIR="running-files/agents"; init.sh:56 runs `cp -R running-files/. docs/` and nothing in init.sh truncates *.jsonl (grep "jsonl" in init.sh finds nothing); check-the-work.sh:849 `verify` FAILS a branch that adds no row to that log, so the kit has to commit a real row there to pass its own step. The templates are empty today (0 bytes), but the next judged kit commit fills them — fix: point the kit's HARNESS_AGENT_DIR at a folder that is not shipped (e.g. a kit-only `agent-logs/`, or a path under the ignored HARNESS_LOG_DIR), and keep running-files/agents/*.jsonl empty; or have init.sh empty docs/agents/*.jsonl after the copy and add an init-test row that asserts it.
F2 [P2] [important] scripts/run-all-gates.sh:224 (header lines 17-25, scripts/README.md:107) — since second-opinion-matrix moved to the slow tier, a `--matrices` run, or a bare run after a harness change, writes a push receipt ("covers: fast") for a tree where the matrices of second-opinion.sh and the 7 new scripts never ran. In v1.6 the fast receipt covered second-opinion-matrix, so this is a regression in push protection for the kit's own scripts — evidence: the 8 slow matrices run only under `if [ "$WANT_FULL" -eq 1 ]`, and the "slow-matrices NOT RUN" line is only printed, never `record`ed, so `manifest_verdict` stays green; lines 287-289 then call harness_receipt_write "fast", and harness_receipt_verify (lib/common.sh ~370) checks only the tree hash, not the tiers. The header still says "--matrices ... force the harness self-test matrices" and "for a push receipt ... pass one of those" — fix: record the slow matrices as skipped in a fast run when HARNESS_TOUCHED=1, so no receipt is written (the way SCOPED_SKIPS works), or make --verify-receipt require `suites` when a slow-matrix script changed; then correct the header and README line 107.
F3 [P3] [important] ci/session-resilience.md:67 — the doc says a missing FINAL report at verify is "NOT CHECKED (exit 4), said loudly, never a pass", but `check-the-work.sh verify` treats hook exit 4 as "go on" and exits 0. With the shipped default HARNESS_REPORT_DIR="" every verify therefore passes with the report contract unchecked — evidence: check-the-work.sh:185 `0|4) ;;`; 20-report-contract.sh verify prints "NOT CHECKED" and runs `exit 4` when neither CTW_REPORT nor HARNESS_REPORT_DIR is set; verify ends with `run_hooks verify` and no non-zero exit — fix: either reword the doc ("verify exits 0; the lead must read the NOT CHECKED line or run `--file` by hand", as parallel-sub-sessions.md:104 already says), or have verify print a closing "INCOMPLETE: report contract not checked" line and exit non-zero.
F4 [P3] [important] scripts/check-the-work.sh:442,908; scripts/check-the-work.d/10-success-criterion.sh:600; scripts/refs-index.py:149 — comments in the ported code name scripts the kit does not ship, as if they were kit scripts. This is a leak from the source project, and it misleads the next reader — evidence: `scripts/check-gate-selfproof.sh` ("how ... calls every check-*.sh") and `scripts/check-superseded-citations.sh` ("its header documents them") do not exist anywhere in the worktree (checked with ls/-e against the whole tree); `scripts/mutation-test.sh` and `scripts/coverage-floors.txt` in the 10-success-criterion.sh:14,147 judge list are harmless as patterns but are also source-project names — fix: reword to the generic case ("a runner that calls a check script with no arguments"; "the citation forms below") or name kit files.
F5 [P3] [nit] scripts/log-agent-run.py:32,56 — ASSUMPTION: the example ids look like source-project specifics left after the neutral renames: `--wave H62`, "such as H63 or EW1", "Docker Desktop hung". They pass the default WAVE_RE, so nothing breaks; the owner can settle it by checking whether H62/H63/EW1 are rows of the source project's runner — fix: use neutral ids such as W8 (already used at line 14).
UNSEEN: I did not run any gate, selftest, init-test or matrix (read-only brief, no writes in the repo), so the PROOF lines and the lead's "all green" claims are unverified. Of the long new scripts I read only the sections a claim pointed at: refs-index.py, review_tally.py, session-state.sh, resume-brief.sh and heavy-run.sh, and most of every *-test.sh matrix, were not read in full. Portability was checked by grep for bash-4/GNU-only constructs (none found), by `/bin/bash -n` (3.2.57) on every new or changed shell script (all parse), and by an ast parse of the three Python files at feature_version 3.8 (all pass); run-time behaviour on Linux was not exercised. The order_files fix (`$(set -f; file_class "$p")`) checked out: file_class's body is byte-identical to ctw_file_class in the hook (cmp), file_class has no other caller, and a cross-author row (check-the-work-test.sh r_order_last_glob_not_expanded_by_the_shell) covers it. I did not watch that row fail before the fix.
